governanceNotes: D1 batch 40 (2026-09-23): two bounded association edges authored. Pain edge: the Papri 2024 prospective cohort of 644 Bangladeshi GBS patients documents pain in 71% during enrollment persisting in 38% at week 13 and 26% at week 26 with chronic pain associated with higher age, male sex, preceding diarrhoea and dysautonomia and with the anxiety/depression quality-of-life domain, the Levison 2020 Danish 30-year nationwide pediatric cohort documents medically treated pain in 70% of chart-reviewed cases mainly confined to the lower extremities, and the Yao 2018 retrospective cohort of 252 acute-phase patients documents pain in 34.5% with a third experiencing pain within the two weeks before weakness onset - a documented acute-to-chronic neuropathic pain profile whose early presentations are frequently unexplained before the neurologic diagnosis lands (case-matching pattern). Category PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL matches the pain-edge precedent family (femoral-neuropathy, episcleritis, erythromelalgia, genitofemoral-nerve-neuralgia, glomus-tumor, flexor-hallucis-longus-tendinitis). Depression edge: the Walteros 2019 prospective cohort of 34 Zika-associated GBS patients assessed at median 17 months documents moderate or moderate-severe depression in GBS survivors at adjusted odds 3.89 versus neighborhood comparison subjects with ongoing disability excess (ODSS at least 1, OR 8.8), the Witsch 2013 nine-center cohort of 110 mechanically ventilated GBS patients assessed at mean 52.6 months documents anxiety/depression-dimension impairment in about half of survivors with long-term quality of life compromised foremost by immobility and chronic pain, and the shared Papri 2024 cohort links chronic pain with the anxiety/depression quality-of-life domain - a psychological-burden association consistent with the depression-precedent family.

Negative screens recorded 2026-09-23: (i) no weakness, paralysis, gait, or respiratory-failure edge - the catalog contains no paralysis, muscle-weakness, difficulty-walking, gait-abnormality, or respiratory-failure identity (the weakness/respiratory keywords resolve to no catalog target), so the core acute motor and ventilatory outcomes have no correct target (wrong-target guard; reopening if governance adds such identities); (ii) no CIDP or chronic-inflammatory-demyelinating-neuropathy conversion edge - A-CIDP conversion is a distinct catalog-relevant diagnostic identity rather than a GBS downstream outcome, and wrong-identity mapping is barred (the batch-40 Shenzhen cohort itself documents three A-CIDP conversions as separate diagnoses); (iii) no cardiac-arrhythmia edge - the located condition-specific record (Dimario 2012 childhood autonomic dysfunction, tachycardia in 77% with 92% recovering by 2-6 months) documents transient acute-phase autonomic manifestations that resolve with recovery rather than a chronic arrhythmia outcome, and no quantified post-GBS chronic-arrhythmia cohort was located (acute-manifestation and zero-record guards); (iv) no peripheral-neuropathy merge - the catalog note directs that GBS not be merged with the generic peripheral-neuropathy identity, which remains zero-edge backlog (wrong-identity and do-not-merge guards); (v) no amputation, deep-vein-thrombosis, pressure-ulcer, or urinary-incontinence edge - immobility-mediated complications lack GBS-specific quantified forward-outcome cohorts in this window (zero-record guard); (vi) duplicate-scope note: campylobacter-jejuni-infection already carries an ASSOCIATION_ONLY incoming edge to GBS (antecedent trigger direction) and this batch adds two outgoing GBS edges - no parallel pathway; unexplained-chronic-pain gains a seventh incoming case-matching edge and depressive-disorder a seventeenth-family psychological incoming edge, each with independent condition-specific evidence bases and no pooled duplication. Reopening conditions: a quantified post-GBS chronic-arrhythmia cohort, a catalog identity for weakness or respiratory failure, or a controlled depression-incidence cohort beyond the located survivor series.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The Papri 2024 prospective cohort of 644 GBS patients documents pain in 71% at enrollment persisting in 38% at week 13 and 26% at week 26 with chronic pain associated with dysautonomia, preceding diarrhoea, higher age, and male sex and with the anxiety/depression quality-of-life domain, the Levison 2020 Danish 30-year nationwide pediatric cohort documents medically treated pain in 70% of cases mainly in the lower extremities, and the Yao 2018 cohort of 252 acute-phase patients documents pain in 34.5% with a third of pain-reporters experiencing pain in the two weeks preceding weakness onset - the literature documents a reproducible acute-to-chronic neuropathic pain profile, frequently the presenting and unexplained complaint before the neurologic diagnosis, without establishing that GBS caused a distinct chronic pain disorder in any individual.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: The mapping does not assert that GBS caused a separate chronic pain disorder: pain is in substantial part a documented feature of the immune-mediated neuropathy itself (radicular and neuropathic pain tracks disease severity and dysautonomia), so the edge records case-matching of presentations - early unexplained pain complaints and persistent post-illness pain whose exclusionary workup mirrors the unexplained-chronic-pain evaluation (femoral-neuropathy and glomus-tumor precedent) - rather than a distinct downstream arrow; fibromyalgia, diabetic or other small-fiber polyneuropathy, musculoskeletal deconditioning pain, radiculopathy, and central post-stroke or post-critical-illness pain independently produce chronic regional pain in the same populations, and residual limb weakness plus immobility confound pain attribution; individual claims require confirmed GBS (clinical criteria with electrodiagnostic or nerve-biopsy support where obtained), documented pain chronology and distribution within the unexplained-chronic-pain identity's scope, and exclusion of the mimickers with the site-appropriate workup documented.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: An immune-mediated sensory-fiber excitation pathway: post-infectious molecular mimicry antibodies attack dorsal-root-ganglion and peripheral nerve structures producing ectopic discharge in injured axons, with residual deafferentation and central sensitization maintaining nociceptive gain after motor recovery - generating radicular and distal neuropathic pain that presents before or outlasts the weakness (26% still reporting pain at week 26) and loops through workups without diagnosis until the neurologic picture consolidates - the documented acute-to-chronic pain profile that grounds the case-matching edge while individual attribution of a distinct pain disorder remains an association hypothesis.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The edge asserts an association only: the located condition-specific evidence is observational cohort data on pain frequency and persistence without any distinct chronic-pain-disorder diagnosis attributable to GBS in an individual, pain is in substantial part constitutive of the neuropathy itself (tracking severity and dysautonomia) so a separate causal arrow risks double-counting the symptom, competing chronic-pain etiologies (fibromyalgia, small-fiber neuropathy, deconditioning, radiculopathy) are common in the same populations, and all case-matching pain precedents rest at NOT_ESTABLISHED; no probability estimate is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Clinical or electrodiagnostically confirmed GBS (Brighton criteria with nerve-conduction studies where obtained) with documented antecedent infection timeline; pain chronology with documented onset (before, during, or after weakness), distribution, and serial severity scores persisting past week 26 within the unexplained-chronic-pain identity's scope; exclusionary workup (nerve-conduction studies or small-fiber testing, glucose tolerance and B12, imaging of the spine) documented; exclusion of fibromyalgia, diabetic or other small-fiber polyneuropathy, musculoskeletal deconditioning pain, radiculopathy, and central post-critical-illness pain; neurology and pain-medicine assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Diabetic, small-fiber, or other metabolic polyneuropathy
Musculoskeletal deconditioning or joint pain after prolonged immobility

evidenceGaps: Clinical or electrodiagnostically confirmed GBS (Brighton criteria with nerve-conduction studies where obtained) with documented antecedent infection timeline; pain chronology with documented onset (before, during, or after weakness), distribution, and serial severity scores persisting past week 26 within the unexplained-chronic-pain identity's scope; exclusionary workup (nerve-conduction studies or small-fiber testing, glucose tolerance and B12, imaging of the spine) documented; exclusion of fibromyalgia, diabetic or other small-fiber polyneuropathy, musculoskeletal deconditioning pain, radiculopathy, and central post-critical-illness pain; neurology and pain-medicine assessment of the individual relationship
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY as a case-matching pain edge on the femoral-neuropathy, glomus-tumor, and genitofemoral precedent: condition-specific cohort data documents a high-frequency acute-to-chronic neuropathic pain profile whose early presentations are unexplained and whose exclusionary workup mirrors the unexplained-chronic-pain evaluation, while the constitutive nature of neuropathy pain, competing chronic-pain etiologies, and absent distinct-disorder attribution keep the consensus at NOT_ESTABLISHED with confirmation and alternative-etiology requirements.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The Walteros 2019 prospective cohort of 34 Zika-associated GBS survivors assessed at a median of 17 months documents moderate or moderate-severe depression at age- and sex-adjusted odds of 3.89 versus neighborhood comparison subjects without GBS alongside persistent disability excess, the Witsch 2013 nine-center cohort of 110 mechanically ventilated GBS patients assessed at mean 52.6 months documents anxiety/depression-dimension impairment in about half of survivors with long-term quality of life compromised foremost by immobility and chronic pain, and the Papri 2024 cohort of 644 patients links chronic pain with the anxiety/depression quality-of-life domain - the literature documents a reproducible depression excess in GBS survivors against comparison populations without establishing that GBS caused a major depressive disorder in any individual.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: The mapping does not assert that GBS caused a distinct depressive disorder in any individual: the depression signal is inseparable from its mediators - persistent disability, chronic pain, immobility, fatigue, and the psychological burden of acute paralysis and ventilation - so the edge records association across the post-illness burden rather than an independent causal arrow (female-infertility and frontal-fibrosizing-alopecia psychological-burden precedent); pre-existing mood disorder, socioeconomic strain, and the single etiology-specific survivor series (Zika-associated) confound attribution, and reverse-direction influence of depression on rehabilitation participation and symptom reporting is plausible; individual claims require confirmed GBS with a structured psychiatric diagnostic assessment (SCID or equivalent) documenting depressive symptoms of grade and duration meeting the depressive-disorder identity's scope, chronology after the neurologic illness, and exclusion of bipolar, substance-induced, medication-induced (corticosteroid, interferon), and thyroid or B12-deficiency mimics per case.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A post-illness psychological-burden pathway: acute immune-mediated paralysis, ICU care and mechanical ventilation, prolonged immobility, neuropathic pain, and fatigue sustain helplessness and loss-of-role stress while cytokine-mediated sickness behavior and disrupted sleep maintain mood dysregulation - producing a depression excess in survivors (adjusted odds near 4 in the located cohort, impairment in about half of ventilated survivors at mean 4.4 years) that tracks disability and chronic pain rather than a discrete endogenous disease process, so individual attribution remains an association hypothesis under the psychological-burden precedent.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The edge asserts an association only: the located condition-specific evidence is a single etiology-specific survivor cohort with comparison subjects (Zika-associated GBS), a ventilated-patient series without a non-GBS control, and cohort quality-of-life domain data rather than any structured diagnostic-incidence study, the depression signal is mediated through disability, pain, and immobility so an independent causal arrow would overstate the direct pathway, psychiatric and reverse-direction confounders are unexcluded, and the psychological-burden depression precedents all rest at NOT_ESTABLISHED; no probability estimate is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Clinical or electrodiagnostically confirmed GBS with documented illness severity, ventilation status, and recovery trajectory; structured psychiatric diagnostic assessment (SCID or equivalent) documenting depressive symptoms of grade and duration meeting the depressive-disorder identity's scope with onset chronology after the neurologic illness; serial disability (GBS disability scale or ODSS), pain, fatigue, and sleep measures documenting the mediating burden; exclusion of pre-existing or recurrent depressive and bipolar disorder, substance-induced mood disorder, corticosteroid- or interferon-induced mood symptoms, and hypothyroidism or B12 deficiency; psychiatry assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Pre-existing or recurrent major depressive or bipolar disorder
Substance-induced or medication-induced (corticosteroid, interferon) mood disorder
Hypothyroidism or vitamin B12 deficiency mimicking fatigue and mood symptoms
Adjustment disorder or grief reactions without meeting depressive-disorder scope
Post-critical-illness cognitive or fatigue syndromes without primary depression

evidenceGaps: Clinical or electrodiagnostically confirmed GBS with documented illness severity, ventilation status, and recovery trajectory; structured psychiatric diagnostic assessment (SCID or equivalent) documenting depressive symptoms of grade and duration meeting the depressive-disorder identity's scope with onset chronology after the neurologic illness; serial disability (GBS disability scale or ODSS), pain, fatigue, and sleep measures documenting the mediating burden; exclusion of pre-existing or recurrent depressive and bipolar disorder, substance-induced mood disorder, corticosteroid- or interferon-induced mood symptoms, and hypothyroidism or B12 deficiency; psychiatry assessment of the individual relationship
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY under the psychological-burden precedent (female-infertility, frontal-fibrosizing-alopecia to depressive-disorder): survivor cohorts document a depression excess against comparison populations and impairment in about half of ventilated survivors at long-term follow-up, while mediation through disability and pain, single-series and no-control limitations, psychiatric and reverse-direction confounders, and precedent norms keep the consensus at NOT_ESTABLISHED with structured-diagnosis and alternative-etiology requirements.
